reading.body:
A data center entry in Phoenix could not be confirmed as an operating facility, and its coordinates resolve to an unrelated garage door company.

The pattern here is a name without a building behind it. Accelera Data Systems appears in OpenStreetMap as a node tagged for data centers, but no operator website, business registration, or press coverage exists for it in Arizona. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates returns A1 Garage Door Service on West Behrend Drive in the Deer Valley area, a home-services business with no connection to the listed name. The address sits roughly 15 to 20 miles from the other eight rows in its batch, so no shared structure ties them together.

For AI infrastructure, the useful signal is negative. A facility with no published specifications cannot be counted toward capacity, and Arizona's four facilities with published power figures total 512 MW. This entry adds nothing to that number and cannot be ranked against it. The absence of a working website and registration is what a genuinely operating colocation or hosting business would not look like.

What the data does not establish is whether a data center ever existed at this location. A stale or imprecise map pin and a vacated address produce the same record as a name that was never real. Confirming either would require independent sources that this research did not find.
